questions.q: In a circuit with two light bulbs connected in parallel, what happens to the second bulb if the first bulb is removed?
questions.a: The second bulb stays lit. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks electricity behaves like a single-lane road (series circuit) where one break stops the entire flow.

questions.q: Why do homes use parallel circuits instead of one single path for all lights and appliances?
questions.a: Homes use parallel circuits so that each appliance can be turned on or off independently and so that a failure in one device (like a bulb) does not cause the entire house to go dark. A wrong answer indicates the student does not understand the benefit of having independent paths.

questions.q: If you connect two bulbs in parallel to a 9V battery, how much voltage does each bulb receive?
questions.a: Each bulb receives the full 9V. A wrong answer suggests the student believes the voltage is "shared" or divided between branches, a common confusion with series circuit behavior.

questions.q: If a circuit has three bulbs in parallel, and you add a fourth bulb in a new parallel branch, what happens to the existing three bulbs?
questions.a: The existing three bulbs remain lit because they still have their own independent paths to the battery. A wrong answer reveals the student assumes that adding components always affects the operation of others, which is not the case in an ideal parallel setup.

questions.q: Is it better to wire a Christmas tree light string in parallel or series if you want the other lights to stay on when one bulb fails?
questions.a: Parallel is better because it ensures that a single failed bulb does not break the circuit for the rest. If a student chooses series, they are failing to apply the concept of "independent paths" to a practical problem.

questions.q: Draw a diagram or describe how you would arrange two bulbs so that if one is unscrewed, the other remains shining.
questions.a: The student must describe two separate loops connected to the same battery terminals. A poor answer would show a single loop (series), indicating a failure to grasp the physical layout of "separate branches."

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A parallel circuit is an electrical ______ where components are connected across the same two points, creating multiple independent paths for the electric current to flow.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever wondered why, if one light bulb in your house burns out, the rest of the ______ in your room stay on?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to predict that if one bulb is removed from a parallel circuit, the other(s) will remain lit, and explain why this happens by identifying the independent paths for the current.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Have you ever ______ why, if one light bulb in your house burns out, the rest of the lights in your room stay on?
